findings.question: q-physics-fluid-mechanics-0009
findings.quote: Total mass with no volume information
findings.problem: All three wrong choices advertise incomplete information with "with no volume information," "with no mass information," or "alone." Only the keyed choice offers a comparison with the fluid. A student can select the only unrestricted, comparative choice from its wording without knowing the density rule.
findings.fix: Use parallel property names without exclusion cues, such as average density, total mass, surface area, and longest dimension, each relative to the fluid or displaced fluid where appropriate.

findings.question: q-physics-fluid-mechanics-0019
findings.quote: This treats the surface as the source of an upward contact force. The surface is a visible boundary. Check force directions from surrounding pressure.
findings.problem: The associated choice says the free surface exerts a downward pull, but this note describes an upward contact force. It therefore misidentifies the selected mistake and does not explain why a downward pull might seem plausible.
findings.fix: Explain that the student imagines the visible surface pulling on the object; water above the object may suggest a downward action. Check that buoyancy is upward and comes from surrounding pressure increasing with depth.
